question_en: The competitive forces identified by Michael Porter include:
option_a: power of existing competitors and threat of entry.
option_b: rivalry among existing competitors and power of buyers.
option_c: threat of substitutes and rivalry among suppliers.
explanation_en: Porter's five competitive forces are: (1) rivalry among existing competitors; (2) threat of entry; (3) threat of substitutes; (4) power of buyers; (5) power of suppliers.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following barriers to entry will increase the competitiveness of the companies within an industry?
explanation_en: The higher the threats to entry, the more competitive the industry becomes. If up-front capital requirements are low, it makes it easier for outside companies to enter the industry and compete with the companies already in the industry. Significant regulatory costs will deter outside companies from trying to enter, as will pre-existing customer loyalties.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following types of industries is typically characterized by stable performance during both expansions and contractions of the business cycle?
explanation_en: A defensive industry is typically characterized by stable performance during both expansions and contractions of the business cycle.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: A firm that pursues a differentiation strategy is most likely to emphasize:
explanation_en: A firm that follows a product or service differentiation strategy needs to emphasize market research to identify needs for which customers are willing to pay a premium. Market share and operating efficiency are more of a focus for firms that pursue a low-cost strategy.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Commercial index providers typically classify companies by:
explanation_en: Commercial providers such as Standard and Poor's and MSCI Barra classify companies according to their principal business activity and the products and services they provide.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Commercial industry classification systems such as the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) typically classify firms according to their:
explanation_en: Commercial providers of industry classification systems such as the GICS classify firms according to principal business activity, such as Consumer Staples, Financial Services, or Health Care.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst studying the defense industry will focus on political influences in a PESTLE analysis for which of the following reasons?
option_a: Defense spending is the number-one priority for governments.
option_b: The primary buyers are governmental entities.
option_c: Political parties determine whether or not to spend on defense.
explanation_en: It is an accurate statement that governments are not only the primary, but also often the only buyers for the defense sector. Defense spending is an important priority, but not necessarily the top priority. Political parties may influence how much is spent on defense, but it is not a question of whether or not to spend on defense.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst develops a style box that categorizes industries based on growth rate and sensitivity to economic business cycles. Which of the following industries will most likely land in the box for (higher) growth and defensive sensitivity to cycles?
explanation_en: The growth rate category can be further classified as mature versus growth. The business cycle sensitivity category can be further classified as cyclical versus defensive. Biotechnology is most likely considered growth and defensive. Utilities are mature and defensive. Crude oil production is mature and cyclical.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: The threat of substitutes is most likely to be low for a firm that:
option_a: operates in a fragmented market with little unused capacity.
option_b: produces a commodity product in an industry with signicant unused capacity.
option_c: produces a dierentiated product with high switching costs.
explanation_en: The threat of competition from substitute products is likely to be low for a firm that produces a differentiated product with high switching costs. Unused capacity and low industry concentration (a fragmented market) tend to intensify rivalry among industry competitors but are not directly related to the threat of substitutes.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: An aggressive price reduction to gain market share is most likely to be associated with a:
explanation_en: Michael Porter identified two competitive strategies: cost leadership and product or service differentiation. A firm that uses a cost leadership or low-cost strategy seeks to have low production costs that will enable it to offer lower prices than its competitors to protect or gain market share. A product or service differentiation strategy seeks to gain a price premium for its products by making them distinctive to the consumer.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Industry analysis is most likely to provide an analyst with insight about a company's:
explanation_en: Industry analysis provides a framework for an analyst to understand a firm in relation to its competitive environment, which determines how much pricing power a firm has. Competitive strategy and financial performance are aspects of company analysis.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Company X runs a series of high-end hotels in the Northeastern United States. The average room rate per night is higher than any other hotel in the region. Which of the following best allows the company to build upon its differentiation strategy?
option_a: Economies of scale and low variable costs.
option_b: Strong cost controls, which allow the company to maintain prot margins.
option_c: A culture of strong customer experience.
explanation_en: A company running high-end hotels with high average room rates is executing a differentiation strategy, where customers see value in paying more for a product or service. A culture of strong customer experience lends itself to this strategy. Economies of scale, low variable costs, and strong cost controls are needed with a cost leadership strategy.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Economic profits are most likely to be earned by firms in an industry that is characterized by:
option_a: low threat of substitutes and high rivalry among existing competitors.
option_b: high barriers to entry and low power of buyers.
option_c: high power of suppliers and low threat of entry.
explanation_en: High barriers to entry (low threat of entry) and low power of buyers both increase the potential for economic profits within an industry. The five forces that shape industry competition are rivalry among existing competitors, threat of entry, threat of substitutes, power of buyers, and power of suppliers. The stronger any of these forces are within an industry, the less potential that industry has to generate (or continue to earn) economic profits.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Food, beverage, and utility companies are examples of:
explanation_en: Food, beverage, and utility companies provide basic necessities of life and are considered to be defensive industries. In a recession, the demand for their products will not fall as much as for some of the other industry groups.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: A commercial industry classification system has a hierarchical structure: economic sectors, business sectors, industry groups, industries, and activities. Which of the following classifications does this represent?
explanation_en: This is the hierarchical structure for the TRBC classification system: economic sectors, business sectors, industry groups, industries, and activities. For ICB, it is this: industries, supersectors, sectors, and subsectors. For GICS, it is this: sector, industry groups, industries, and subindustries.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Regarding competitive strategy and Porter's Five Forces, the bargaining power of customers can be overcome by successfully implementing which type of strategy?
explanation_en: Firms implementing all three strategies (cost leadership, differentiation, and focus) may overcome the bargaining power of customers. Cost leadership firms can benefit by the customers' inability to drive down prices beyond the costs of the marginal producer. Differentiation firms and focus firms can take advantage of the customers' inability or unwillingness to shop around or switch suppliers.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: Factors that increase competition in an industry most likely include:
option_a: low barriers to entry, high concentration, and high unused capacity.
option_b: low barriers to entry, low concentration, and high unused capacity.
option_c: high barriers to entry, low concentration, and low unused capacity.
explanation_en: Low barriers to entry increase competition as more firms can enter the business. Industries that are fragmented and have unused capacity tend to be highly competitive as they fight for market share and attempt to utilize excess manufacturing resources.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst studying an industry notices that the rivalries among the companies in the industry are fairly significant. Which of the following characteristics of the industry supports the analyst's assessment?
option_a: Fixed costs are low relative to variable costs.
option_b: The costs to exit the market exceed the costs of staying in.
explanation_en: When the costs to exit a market exceed the costs of staying in, the industry's competitiveness is more significant because companies are "stuck." Unique product offerings and low fixed costs ease (rather than accentuate) competitiveness.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: In an industry and competitive analysis, the industry base rate is best described as the:
option_a: average market share for each company within an industry.
option_b: maximum number of companies an industry can support.
option_c: overall baseline protability for the industry as a whole.
explanation_en: While individual companies may have greater (or lesser) profitability than their industry overall for a period of time, eventually, they will move toward the industry base rate— which is a measure of the overall baseline profitability for the industry as a whole. The base rate is not the maximum number of companies in an industry or the average market share for each company within an industry.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 46 Industry and Competitive Analysis - Answers.pdf
question_en: As part of an industry and competitive analysis, an analyst first defines and then surveys an industry. Which of the following assessments will be made as part of the survey step?
option_a: The growth rate of the industry over the last several years.
option_b: Political and economic impacts on the industry.
option_c: The geographical region in which the industry operates.
explanation_en: Surveying the industry involves assessing its size, profitability, growth, and market share trends. Political and economic impacts are evaluated as part of the examine external influences step, while the geographical region is assessed in the define the industry step.
